```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)
set.seed(123)
```

## 1. Question and data

**Question:** in a hospital isolate collection, which bacteria are most common,
how resistant are they to key antibiotics, does resistance differ between wards
and over time, and what share of isolates are multidrug-resistant?

**Data:** the `example_isolates` dataset shipped with the `AMR` package: 2,000
bacterial isolates with their antibiograms (susceptibility results as S, I or R),
plus date, patient, age, gender and ward. It is an example dataset for the
package, so the results illustrate the workflow and should not be read as real
surveillance findings.

```{r libs}
library(AMR)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r data}
iso <- example_isolates
iso$species <- mo_name(iso$mo)
iso$gram <- mo_gramstain(iso$mo)
iso$year <- as.integer(format(iso$date, "%Y"))

dim(iso)
range(iso$date)
table(iso$ward)
```

## 2. Keep one isolate per patient episode

Surveillance counts should not include repeat isolates from the same patient,
because they inflate resistance rates. `first_isolate()` keeps the first
isolate of each patient and species episode.

```{r first}
iso$first <- first_isolate(iso)
fi <- iso[which(iso$first), ]
cat("All isolates:", nrow(iso), "\n")
cat("First isolates kept:", nrow(fi), "\n")
```

## 3. Which pathogens are most common?

```{r species}
top_species <- fi %>%
  count(species, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  head(10)
top_species

ggplot(top_species, aes(x = reorder(species, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2a9d8f") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "First isolates")
```

```{r gram}
fi %>%
  count(gram) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
```

## 4. Antibiograms

A traditional antibiogram gives the percentage of isolates susceptible (S or I)
per species and antibiotic. Combinations that cover more isolates are useful
for empiric therapy.

```{r antibiogram}
antibiogram(fi, antibiotics = c("AMX", "AMC", "CIP", "GEN", "TZP"))
```

Combination antibiogram by Gram stain: does adding an aminoglycoside to
piperacillin/tazobactam improve coverage?

```{r combo}
antibiogram(fi, antibiotics = c("TZP", "TZP+GEN", "TZP+TOB"),
            mo_transform = "gramstain")
```

## 5. Resistance in *Escherichia coli* by ward

```{r ward}
ecoli <- fi %>% filter(species == "Escherichia coli")
abx <- c("AMX", "AMC", "CIP", "GEN", "SXT")

res_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(abx, function(ab) {
  ecoli %>%
    mutate(r = as.character(.data[[ab]])) %>%
    filter(!is.na(r)) %>%
    group_by(ward) %>%
    summarise(antibiotic = ab, tested = n(), resistant = sum(r == "R"),
              .groups = "drop")
}))

res_tbl <- res_tbl %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(pct = 100 * resistant / tested,
         lo = 100 * prop.test(resistant, tested)$conf.int[1],
         hi = 100 * prop.test(resistant, tested)$conf.int[2]) %>%
  ungroup()

res_tbl %>% mutate(across(c(pct, lo, hi), ~ round(.x, 1)))

ggplot(res_tbl, aes(x = ward, y = pct, fill = ward)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~antibiotic, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% resistant (95% CI)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## 6. Resistance trend over time

Ciprofloxacin resistance in *E. coli*, modelled with logistic regression on
calendar year. The odds ratio is per additional year.

```{r trend}
trend_df <- ecoli %>%
  mutate(r = as.character(CIP)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(r)) %>%
  mutate(resistant = as.integer(r == "R"),
         year_c = year - min(year))

yearly <- trend_df %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(tested = n(), pct_resistant = 100 * mean(resistant))
yearly

fit_trend <- glm(resistant ~ year_c, data = trend_df, family = binomial)
trend_or <- exp(cbind(OR_per_year = coef(fit_trend), confint.default(fit_trend)))
round(trend_or, 3)
summary(fit_trend)$coefficients

# Fitted curve with 95% CI from the logistic model (on the link scale)
newd <- data.frame(year_c = 0:max(trend_df$year_c))
pr <- predict(fit_trend, newdata = newd, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
newd$year <- newd$year_c + min(trend_df$year)
newd$fit <- 100 * plogis(pr$fit)
newd$lo <- 100 * plogis(pr$fit - 1.96 * pr$se.fit)
newd$hi <- 100 * plogis(pr$fit + 1.96 * pr$se.fit)

ggplot(yearly, aes(x = year, y = pct_resistant)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = newd, aes(x = year, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#e76f51", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = newd, aes(x = year, y = fit),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#e76f51", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(size = tested)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "% ciprofloxacin-resistant", size = "Isolates tested")
```

## 7. Factors associated with ciprofloxacin resistance

Age is split at 65 years. A first version with three age groups gave unstable
estimates (odds ratios in the hundreds of thousands), a sign of quasi-complete
separation: some small groups had no resistant isolates, so the model could not
estimate an odds ratio. The cross-tabulation below shows the counts.

```{r logit}
trend_df$age_group <- factor(ifelse(trend_df$age >= 65, "65+", "<65"),
                             levels = c("<65", "65+"))
table(age_group = trend_df$age_group, resistant = trend_df$resistant)
table(ward = trend_df$ward, resistant = trend_df$resistant)

fit <- glm(resistant ~ ward + gender + age_group, data = trend_df,
           family = binomial)
round(exp(cbind(OR = coef(fit), confint.default(fit))), 2)
```

## 8. Multidrug-resistant organisms (MDR)

`mdro()` classifies each isolate by international consensus definitions
(default: Magiorakos et al. 2012, CMI).

```{r mdro}
fi$mdr <- mdro(fi)
table(fi$mdr)

mdr_ward <- fi %>%
  count(ward, mdr) %>%
  group_by(ward) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ungroup()
mdr_ward

ggplot(mdr_ward, aes(x = ward, y = percent, fill = mdr)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of first isolates", fill = "Class")
```

## 9. Export

```{r export}
dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(res_tbl, "results/ecoli_resistance_by_ward.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(yearly, "results/ecoli_cip_resistance_by_year.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(mdr_ward, "results/mdr_by_ward.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## 10. Limitations

- The data are an example dataset shipped with a software package, so the numbers
  illustrate the workflow and are not real surveillance results.
- Some species-antibiotic-ward groups have few isolates, so confidence intervals
  are wide.
- The trend model is a simple logistic regression and ignores changes in testing
  practice over time.
- Resistance is reported for first isolates only; clinical breakpoints and
  intrinsic resistance rules follow the `AMR` package defaults.
